title: Client KV coalescing and action commit playbook
body:
Context
We keep getting ambiguous failure modes when streaming results + tool calls intersect with client-side caching. This doc proposes a minimal proto for client-side KV caching + action coalescing and a small commit/abort handshake so SDKs can resume streams, dedupe retries, and present a simple mental model to app developers.

Goals
- Keep SDK surface tiny: two primitives (coalesce(key, op), commit(id) + abort(id)).
- Make resume/idempotency reliable across intermittent connectivity and server-side fallbacks.
- Preserve streaming latency for the common fast-path (no commit required for ephemeral responses).
- Provide telemetry hooks to measure coalescing efficiency, commit latency and conflict rates.

Design summary
1) Client KV cache: small persistent map (key -> pending-op-record). Keys are developer-provided (e.g. user-id + prompt-hash) or auto-generated by SDK when using session fragments. The SDK exposes coalesce(key, op) which returns a local promise-like handle. If a pending-op exists, the SDK attaches to the same inflight.

2) Action coalescing: ops that map to identical model/tool invocations (same model+params+input) should be joined. For tool-calls that have side effects, coalesce only when developer marks op as "safe-to-coalesce".

3) Commit/Abort handshake: for any op that caused external side effects (DB writes, provider tool invocations), server returns an op_id in initial partial response frame. Client calls commit(op_id) once it has reached app-level acceptance. If connection dies, commit can be retried. If server receives duplicate commit for already-committed op_id, it returns 200 with idempotent response. Abort indicates client decided to abandon the action; server can garbage-collect and attempt cleanup.

4) Streaming implications: initial partial frames should contain a short op header {op_id, coalesce_key?, safe_flag}. SDK writes these to KV cache immediately so resumed sessions can request op state by op_id and attach to inflight.

API sketch (JS-like)
- const h = await client.coalesce('user:123:rev42', () => client.generate({...})); // returns handle to stream
- h.on('delta', cb)
- h.on('end', () => client.commit(h.op_id))
- client.abort(h.op_id) // optional

Telemetry and observability
- emit metrics: coalesce.attach_rate, coalesce.miss_rate, commit.latency_ms, commit.conflicts, resume.attach_success
- tracing: span for op_id across client and server; include coalesce_key and model.id in tags

Edge cases and failure modes
- Stale cache entry: SDK TTL default 5 minutes; apps can override. On attach after TTL expiry, SDK treats as miss and starts new op (old op kept server-side until GC).
- Conflicting commits: server performs lightweight compare-and-swap; if conflict, API returns 409 with current status. SDK should surface as structured error to app with suggested remediation (attach-to-current or user-retry).
- Offline-first: SDK persists pending-op-records to disk; on reconnect attempts to re-attach before starting a fresh invocation.

Migration plan
- Phase 0: opt-in behind SDK flag (alpha). telemetry-only mode to collect coalescing signals.
- Phase 1: beta: expose coalesce API and commit/abort semantics; integrate into streaming SDKs for mobile and node.
- Phase 2: opt-in server-side tooling: honor coalesce keys for hosted inference to reduce duplicate compute.

Open questions
- Should server limit coalescing window beyond client TTL? (tradeoff between memory and dedupe win).
- How to represent partial tool-call state when tool-run includes multiple downstream jobs?
- UX: do we expose coalesce_key generation helpers or force app to own keys?

Next steps / TODOs
- (Ethan) mock the server op header in streaming frames (PR link above).
- (Maya) prototype JS SDK attachments and persistence.
- (Priya) run a canary on a low-traffic workspace to measure coalesce hit rate.

Notes to reviewers
This is intentionally compact — aim for a pragmatic workstream. Comments welcome on naming (op_id vs tx_id) and whether commit should be synchronous by default or return a confirmation pollable via status endpoint.
